Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8489-kanban-empty-badge-label`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and ⛔ never writes the assignee field.

## Why this one is dispatched straight

No ruling is open. An **empty, fully-styled coloured pill** is not a defensible rendering of anything, the card measured it **by rendering** rather than by reading, and it names the repair shape itself:

> Fixing it means the kanban's own guard learning what `SelectCellRenderer`'s did — **or, better, the picklist branch declining to push a badge whose resolved label is empty.**

⭐ **Take the second.** It is strictly narrower, it needs no knowledge of what an "empty value" is, and it closes the second half too (below). ⛔ If your measurement says otherwise, report it — but do not reimplement an emptiness judgement inside `ObjectKanban` when the question at that point is only *"is there a label to draw?"*

## ⭐ The second half is the real scope, and it is independent of arrays

> **any** value that resolves to an empty label — an option whose declared `label` is the empty string, a stored value that stringifies to nothing — produces the same empty pill. The array case is simply the one that is easy to hit.

⇒ a fix that special-cases `[]` **leaves the defect standing** and will read as complete. ⚠️ **The discriminating pin is a non-array value that resolves to an empty label**, not the empty array. Build the fixture that way and the array case comes along for free; build it the other way round and it does not.

## What the card established — re-derive, but do not re-litigate

`packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx:604` opens the explicit-card-field loop with `if (raw == null || raw === '') continue;` — **`[]` passes that guard** — and four lines later forks on `isPicklist`, which is true for **any field carrying declared `options`**. That branch never calls `getCellRenderer`, so objectui#8481's renderer fix **cannot reach it**: it resolves a label and colour itself and pushes a plain object onto `cardBadges`.

Measured by rendering a real board with objectui#8481 applied: `tags` (declares options) → **an indigo pill with zero children**; `topics` (no options) and `owners` → the shared `No value` affordance. ⇒ ⭐ **the broken one is the most commonly authored shape**, because a picklist that declares its options is the normal case.

⚠️ Line numbers are from `7cf6f38fb`. **Re-locate by content** and report what you found — objectui#8665 and objectui#8703 were each half or wholly falsified tonight because a source reading was taken for a behavioural one. The rendering measurement here is sound; the addresses are not facts.

## Evidence bar

1. ⭐ **Leg 1**: render the board today and show the empty pill — **both** for `[]` **and** for a non-array value resolving to an empty label. ⛔ Reproduce before repairing.
2. the fix draws no badge for either, while every populated badge is **byte-identical** to today;
3. ⭐ **non-regression, derived from the plausible wrong fix**: *"drop any badge whose label is falsy"* would also drop a legitimately authored **`'0'`** label, and *"drop empty arrays"* leaves the second half standing. **Pin a `'0'`-labelled option rendering normally**, and pin the empty-label case separately.
4. **caricature both ways**: *"never push a badge"* and *"always push a badge"* — both must redden loudly.

⚠️ **An assertion never observed to fail has not been tested.** Every pin must be observed red under leg 3 or leg 4.

- ⚠️ ⭐ **Assert the badge's absence at the DOM, not at `cardBadges`.** A pin on the array is one refactor away from meaning nothing, and the defect is what the card *draws*.
- ⚠️ `queryByText('')` will not do what you want, and `queryByText` throws on **multiple** matches as well as none. Count nodes at a stable selector — and ⚠️ **verify each selector matches exactly one node per badge**: `.rounded-full` matches **TWO** nodes per avatar elsewhere in this repo (Radix `Avatar.Root` **and** `AvatarFallback`), which objectui#8596's census never noticed because it navigated with `querySelector` instead of counting.
- **Ablation:** mutate a READ SITE (never a pin), from a committed tree, `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths, proving the mutation on disk **in both directions** (anchor counts AND `git hash-object` vs the HEAD blob) **plus a line-total gate**; restore **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty; `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`, never the bare form). **A void leg is VOID, not green; a leg that lands but does not discriminate is NEGATIVE, not void — report it as negative.**
- ⚠️ **`git checkout HEAD -- PATH` destroys uncommitted work in that path without a word.** Commit your own edits first — that cost a redo on PR #8713 tonight.
- **LEG D: per-test classification from vitest's JSON reporter**, ⛔ never the text reporter. Count death strings separately.

## Scope

- ⛔ **`ObjectKanban`'s badge branch only.** Do not touch `@object-ui/fields`' renderers — objectui#8481 owns those and its fix is landed.
- ⚠️ **objectui#8534** (`KanbanImpl` mirrors its `columns` prop into state and repaints one frame of empty columns) is the same package, **a different defect, and not dispatched.** ⛔ Do not fold it in; if your fixture trips over it, say so.
- ⚠️ **DOM shapes in your report should be spelled in words, not written literally** — tag-shaped fragments are eaten from GitHub bodies even inside backticks. The card does this deliberately.

## objectui traps (measured, carry them)

- Run vitest **from the repo root with paths**. Guard objectui#3378 refuses `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE`; `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently re-roots onto `apps/console`. ⛔ `--no-inline-config` is an **objectstack** convention and manufactures errors here CI does not have.
- ⚠️ happy-dom reports `clientWidth: 0` and never fires container-size effects; **RTL's `asyncWrapper` drains one macrotask before returning**, so a `setTimeout(…, 0)` deferral sits inside its own drain window (use 50ms if you need one).
- ⚠️ Type-check with the dependency closure built; an unbuilt tree gives `TS2307` for every workspace import — a **PRECONDITION**, recorded **NOT MEASURED**.
- ⚠️ **`.at(-1)` is TS2550** in packages inheriting the root `lib: ["ES2020"]` (objectui#8691); jest-dom matchers are typed program-wide by whichever file imports them (objectui#8722) — ⚠️ so a matcher that compiles in your package may do so **only because another file imports jest-dom**.
- ⚠️ `search_issues` returns **false zeros** here and REST `/search/issues` has answered **403 including its control**. Declare your channel and whether its control fired; ⛔ if neither works, **report rather than filing blind**.
- `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**; the real exemption is an **empty-frontmatter** changeset — get the gate's **own verdict line**.

## Collisions

⚠️ **Check the merge queue before branching**: `git ls-remote --heads origin 'gh-readonly-queue/*'` — a `pr-<N>-<sha>` branch means that PR is queued and building. ⛔ Nothing queued touches `plugin-kanban`; keep it that way and **stop and report** if your change reaches a queued PR's files.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8733 is out of draft and armed. No open questions to rule on.

## ⭐ A second push site the card did not name

> **both** `cardBadges.push` sites now decline a badge whose resolved label is empty: the dispatched explicit-`cardFields` picklist branch, **and** — as a bounded same-class in-place fix — **the legacy semantic-field heuristic that runs when a board authors no `cardFields`**, which resolves its label identically, **had the identical defect (reproduced)**, and **would have left the pill drawable from one branch away.**

⇒ fixing only the dispatched branch would have shipped a repair that looks complete and leaves the defect reachable on the **default** path — a board that authors no `cardFields` is not an edge case. Correctly folded in rather than filed: same class, same file, same resolution, and the fix is the same one line of intent.

## ⭐⭐ A sub-premise of the card corrected — and it was a route I put in the dispatch

The card listed **two** routes to an empty label, and my claim comment repeated them. Measured:

> an option whose declared `label` is the empty string **cannot on its own** produce an empty label, because `opt?.label || String(raw)` **falls back to the stringified value** — and the i18n hop cannot introduce one either: `useObjectLabel`'s `resolve()` **rejects a translation equal to the empty string** and returns its fallback.

⇒ **the empty label always arrives via `String(raw)`**, so there is exactly one route, not two. ⭐ I asked for a pin on a case that **cannot occur**; a dev who wrote it would have shipped a test that can never fail — which is this session's own headline defect, in a pin I specified. Measuring the route instead of pinning it is the right handling, and the card's central finding is **untouched**: the empty pill and the array-independence of the second half are both confirmed by rendering.

## ⭐⭐⭐ LEG 3a: my "plausible wrong fix" is not wrong here, and that is reported as NEGATIVE

> *'drop any badge whose label is falsy'*: mutation **LANDED** (blob changed, anchors flipped, line-delta 0) but **9/9 passed** ⇒ reported as **NEGATIVE — not green, and not void.** Cause, **measured**: at this site `!label` and `label === ''` are **behaviourally equivalent**, because `opt?.label || String(raw)` lets no falsy label through, so **the only falsy label reachable at the push IS the empty string.** *"The 'plausible wrong fix' is not in fact wrong here."*

I derived that axis and demanded a `'0'` pin against it. It does not discriminate — and rather than quietly dropping the leg or reporting a false green, the report **names it negative, explains why, keeps `=== ''` as the intent-revealing spelling, and gets the `'0'` pin observed red under leg 4a instead.**

⚠️ That is the **third** non-regression axis of mine measured and found not to hold tonight, and the third time a dev has said so instead of manufacturing agreement. ⭐ The axis was still worth stating — it is what produced the measurement that the two spellings are equivalent *here*, which is a fact about this call site nobody had.

## ⭐ LEG 3b is the discriminating leg, and it vindicates the fixture instruction

> *'drop empty arrays only'*: **7 passed / 2 FAILED — both NON-ARRAY pins red, both array pins green.**

⇒ exactly the outcome the dispatch was built around: *"a fix special-cased on the empty array would have read as complete."* The fixture is built the right way round, and this leg is the proof rather than the claim.

**All nine pins observed red** under leg 3 or leg 4, no void legs, and **byte identity measured rather than asserted** — `POPULATED_BADGE_HTML` **captured from a pre-repair run** and compared against post-repair markup. A "nothing else moved" claim backed by bytes from before the change is the strongest available form.

## ⭐ The selector hazard was applied and then refined

I warned that `.rounded-full` matches **two** nodes per avatar in this repo. The response is better than compliance:

> the selector is **PROVED to match exactly one node per badge** by a census case asserting the populated card's badge-text list — it uses the badge primitive's base classes (`inline-flex` and `whitespace-nowrap` **with** `rounded-full`), **which the two avatar nodes that make a bare `rounded-full` count double do not carry.**

⇒ the hazard is not avoided by hoping, it is **excluded by construction and asserted**. Counts are scoped per card through `SortableCard`'s own accessible-name handle, and `queryByText('')` is correctly identified as unable to express *"no pill"* at all.

## Gates

`eslint .` over the **whole repo** (4594 files, 0 errors) ⇒ **no narrowing needed and none declared** — the honest form when the full population is affordable. Type-check with the dependency closure built first, and the new test file **proved in the program** by `--listFiles` (absent from the main `tsc` program, present in `tsconfig.test.json`'s, and `type-check` runs both) — an excluded test file would have been NOT MEASURED, not a pass. Control bytes scanned by the gate **and** by hand over the three changed files.

⭐ And a **real patch changeset** rather than an empty-frontmatter one, correctly: this changes what a published package renders. `skip-changeset` not applied — phantom label. **0 MCP calls.**

⛔ objectui#8534 not folded in and the fixture did not trip over it; `@object-ui/fields` untouched.
